forward_vs_spot.interpretation: Forward points are derived rather than quoted and are flagged as such: no free source for USD/NOK forward points was obtainable, so all three outrights are built from the cached futures-implied roll premium of 56.5 basis points annualised on an actual-over-365 basis at 30, 91 and 182 days. On that basis the forwards say nothing but the interest rate differential, which is the textbook no-arbitrage outcome and contains no view. The tradeable content is entirely in the gap between the forward and our expectation, and the sign of that gap flips between one and three months, which is the cleanest quantitative statement of the cross-horizon split in the whole dossier: 1020 pips of edge for the bearish view at one month, 2200 pips of edge for the bullish view at six.

key_catalysts.rationale: The prior reading was NOK 266.8bn and the cached OECD ratio is 15.59 per cent of GDP, the largest in the G10 plus SGD set. A large print confirms the structural surplus but also confirms the petroleum revenue that flips the government's foreign exchange leg to buying, so the currency read is genuinely ambiguous. The release rarely moves spot on the day and matters mainly as an input to the strategic external factor.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced as an event; the level is well understood and consensus is unpublished.
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: EUR/NOK and CAD/NOK as the petro-currency comparison

key_catalysts.event: Bank of Canada and Reserve Bank of New Zealand decisions
key_catalysts.rationale: Both are expected to hold, at 2.25 and 2.50 per cent respectively, leaving the krone's 200 and 175 basis point advantages intact. Neither is a krone event in its own right, but the Bank of Canada matters for the cleanest relative-value pair in the dossier because CAD/NOK is the pure petro-currency expression with the oil beta cancelled.

key_catalysts.event: Norway house price index, August (year on year)
key_catalysts.rationale: The prior reading was plus 2.2 per cent year on year, and Norges Bank explicitly flagged on 13 August that secondary housing market prices fell markedly in July. A second weak print would reinforce the case that the September rate path is revised down, because housing is the transmission channel Norges Bank watches most closely for the domestic demand consequences of a 4.25 per cent policy rate.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced. No consensus is published and the market is not positioned for a housing-driven dovish revision.
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: EUR/NOK primarily; NOK/SEK as the Scandinavian housing comparison

key_catalysts.event: Norway manufacturing production, month on month
key_catalysts.rationale: The prior reading was minus 1.0 per cent. Manufacturing is a small share of mainland output and the series is volatile, so a single print is unlikely to move the policy debate. It matters cumulatively as evidence for or against Norges Bank's observation that capacity utilisation is close to normal but drifting down.

key_catalysts.event: Norway producer price index, year on year
key_catalysts.rationale: The prior reading was plus 23.4 per cent year on year, a number dominated by energy price base effects rather than by underlying cost pressure. A high print reads as inflationary in the headline and as a terms-of-trade gain in the balance of payments, and those two readings point in opposite directions for the krone once the fund's sterilisation mechanism is accounted for.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced. The series is widely ignored precisely because its energy weighting makes it hard to interpret.

key_catalysts.event: Norway CPI and CPI-ATE, August (Statistics Norway)
key_catalysts.rationale: The single most important Norwegian data release in the window. July printed headline 3.0 per cent and CPI-ATE 2.7 per cent, the second consecutive 2.7 per cent core reading and below the June projection. A third print at or below 2.7 per cent makes a downward revision to the 24 September path close to unavoidable, and because market pricing and the bank's own path are aligned to roughly three basis points, that revision hits both simultaneously. Headline year on year, core month on month and core year to date all publish together.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Partially priced at best. Roughly 27 basis points of tightening remains priced across the rest of 2026 and the 12-month generic sits 31 basis points above the policy rate, so the market has not yet discounted a third soft core print. We estimate 8 to 12 basis points would come out of the 12-month generic on a print at or below 2.6 per cent.
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: EUR/NOK first, then NOK/SEK and USD/NOK

key_catalysts.event: European Central Bank Governing Council decision with staff projections
key_catalysts.rationale: The most consequential scheduled event for the krone's carry. A 25 basis point hike to 2.50 per cent is priced at approximately 80 per cent at the cited source, with 86 to 99 per cent quoted elsewhere, and roughly even odds attach to a further move to 2.75 per cent in December. A hike compresses the krone's 200 basis point advantage over the euro to 175 basis points immediately and toward 150 by year-end, which reverses the direction of the differential that has driven the krone all year.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Approximately 80 per cent priced at the cited source and higher elsewhere - the dispersion is itself flagged. The hike is therefore largely in the price; what is not priced is the December follow-through and the compounding effect on the differential.
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: EUR/NOK above all; indirectly NOK/SEK through the European rate complex

key_catalysts.rationale: The prior reading was a surplus of NOK 84.3bn, the largest in four months, on exports of NOK 173.6bn against imports of NOK 89.3bn. Another large surplus confirms the terms-of-trade strength that has supported the krone narrative and simultaneously confirms the petroleum revenue that keeps Norges Bank buying foreign exchange for the fund - the central ambiguity of the entire krone case.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced as an event. The market reads a large surplus as unambiguously krone-positive, which is the mis-specification this dossier identifies.

key_catalysts.event: Federal Open Market Committee decision with Summary of Economic Projections
key_catalysts.rationale: The Committee held at 3.50 to 3.75 per cent on 29 July on a 9-3 vote, with Hammack, Kashkari and Logan dissenting in favour of a hike - the first three-way unified hawkish dissent since September 2016. A Summary of Economic Projections that lifts the dots would drive the dollar toward the US-exceptionalism side of the smile, which is the wrong side for an illiquid high-beta currency; one that does not would extend the soft-dollar regime that has supported the krone all year.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Priced as a hold with no change to the dots. The three hawkish dissents mean the market is assigning too little probability to an upward revision in the projections.
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: USD/NOK directly; EUR/NOK through the dollar leg

key_catalysts.event: Bank of England Monetary Policy Committee decision
key_catalysts.rationale: Expected to hold at 3.75 per cent, leaving the krone's 50 basis point advantage intact. Sterling matters to the krone mainly through the fiscal-quality channel - Norway yields 71.2 basis points less than the United Kingdom at ten years despite a 50 basis point higher policy rate, which is the widest expression of relative fiscal quality in the set.

key_catalysts.event: Bank of Japan Monetary Policy Meeting
key_catalysts.rationale: Expected to hold at 1.00 per cent with a gradual normalisation bias intact. The krone's 325 basis point advantage over the yen is the second widest in the set, but NOK/JPY sits at the 95th percentile of its 52-week close distribution with zero weeks since the last close above its 200-week average, so any hawkish surprise would hit an extremely crowded cross.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Fully priced as a hold; the normalisation path is the live question rather than this meeting.
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: NOK/JPY, the most extended cross in the set

key_catalysts.event: Norges Bank policy rate decision with Monetary Policy Report 3/26
key_catalysts.rationale: The largest single event in the tactical window and the transition point between the two horizons. Norges Bank publishes a new projected rate path for the first time since June, when it put the policy rate just above 4.50 per cent at end-2026. Since then two consecutive CPI-ATE prints at 2.7 per cent, a mainland GDP miss, markedly falling house prices, capacity utilisation drifting down and an import-weighted krone at its strongest since autumn 2022 all argue for a downward revision. Because the bank conditions its forecast on the I-44, the krone's own strength is an argument for cutting the path.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced as a revision. The market prices approximately 27 basis points of tightening, essentially matching the June path, so it is positioned for confirmation rather than revision. We assess a downward revision as more likely than not and worth 10 to 15 basis points on the 12-month generic.

key_catalysts.event: Swiss National Bank quarterly assessment and Riksbank Monetary Policy Report
key_catalysts.rationale: The Swiss National Bank is expected to hold at zero and the Riksbank at 1.75 per cent, leaving the krone's 425 and 250 basis point advantages intact. Both matter for the two most extended crosses in the set: CHF/NOK sits at the first percentile of its 52-week close distribution and NOK/SEK at the 100th, so a surprise at either meeting would hit a crowded position.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Fully priced as holds at both.

key_catalysts.event: Reserve Bank of Australia Monetary Policy Board decision
key_catalysts.rationale: Expected to hold at 4.35 per cent, preserving the only positive rate differential against the krone in the entire set - Australia out-yields Norway by 10 basis points. AUD/NOK is correspondingly the one genuinely trendless cross among the ten and is the natural neutral in a krone book.

key_catalysts.event: Norges Bank announces October foreign exchange transactions
key_catalysts.rationale: Announced at 10:00 on the last business day of the month. This is the event that determines whether the September reversal - net purchases of foreign exchange of NOK 176 million per day, a krone offer - was a one-month artefact or the start of a regime. A continuation of foreign currency buying on the government leg would confirm that Norway's terms-of-trade boom is mechanically producing krone selling; a reversion to selling foreign exchange would restore the mechanical bid.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced at all in advance, by construction - the schedule is unknown until it is published. The market has historically under-reacted to it even after publication.
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: EUR/NOK and USD/NOK equally; the flow is not pair-specific

key_catalysts.event: Federal Open Market Committee decision (no projections)
key_catalysts.rationale: Expected to hold. Without a Summary of Economic Projections the meeting carries less information content than 16 September, and its relevance to the krone is confined to whether the balance-sheet stance - stable at USD 6,730,912m as at 26 August 2026, plus 0.3 per cent year on year - is reaffirmed.

key_catalysts.event: European Central Bank Governing Council decision
key_catalysts.rationale: The follow-up to the 10 September meeting. If September delivers the priced hike, this meeting is where the market decides whether December brings another, which is the difference between a krone-euro differential of 175 and 150 basis points at year-end.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Roughly even odds are attached to a further move by December, so this meeting is genuinely two-sided.

key_catalysts.event: Norges Bank policy rate decision (no Monetary Policy Report)
key_catalysts.rationale: An interim decision with no new forecasts, which historically means a low probability of action and a high weight on the wording. The specific question by November is whether the autumn wage settlements have delivered the 4.4 per cent front-line framework, which is the strongest remaining argument that core inflation stops falling in the mid-twos.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Priced as a hold. The wording rather than the decision is the tradeable content.

key_catalysts.event: Norges Bank policy rate decision with Monetary Policy Report 4/26
key_catalysts.rationale: The final scheduled Norwegian event inside the strategic horizon and the point at which the June path's implied hike to just above 4.50 per cent either happens or is formally abandoned. It is also the meeting at which the market would first price 2027 cuts if core inflation has broken below 2.5 per cent.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced. Market attention is concentrated on September, and December pricing will be set by the intervening data.

invalidators.condition: If August CPI-ATE prints at or above 2.9 per cent on 10 September 2026, would turn the tactical stance Bullish because it restores the hiking bias, validates the 31 basis points embedded in the 12-month generic and removes the downward-revision case for the 24 September Monetary Policy Report.
invalidators.mechanism: A firm core print reverses the direction of the Norwegian rate path debate at the same time the European Central Bank is compressing the differential from the other side, so the krone regains the differential argument it currently lacks.

invalidators.condition: If the European Central Bank holds at 2.25 per cent on 10 September 2026 rather than delivering the roughly 80 per cent priced hike, would turn the tactical stance Bullish because the krone's 200 basis point advantage over the euro survives intact and the central plank of the carry-compression case is removed.

invalidators.monitor_frequency: Per meeting for the decision; daily for the pricing

invalidators.mechanism: An upward revision by a credible bank against soft data is the strongest possible signal about its reaction function, and it would reprice the entire Norwegian front end higher at a moment when every other European curve is flat or falling.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: The projected policy rate path in Monetary Policy Report 3/26 against the June path of just above 4.50 per cent at end-2026
invalidators.monitor_frequency: Quarterly, at each Monetary Policy Report

factors_changed.reason: The direction of the differential turned. In the August dossier the krone's 200 basis point advantage over the euro was framed as stable; the 10 September European Central Bank meeting is now roughly 80 per cent priced for a hike, so the differential compresses rather than holds.

Two consecutive CPI-ATE prints at 2.7 per cent and a mainland GDP miss are disinflationary, but the 4.4 per cent front-line wage frame is now given its proper weight as a two- to four-quarter counterweight rather than being treated as a hard ceiling on wage growth.

The decisive change in the cycle. Norges Bank's net transactions reversed by NOK 650 million per day effective 1 September, from a NOK 474 million per day krone bid to a NOK 176 million per day krone offer. This is now the highest-confidence single input in the dossier.
The same reversal, plus the recognition that the fund's sterilisation mechanism means a stronger terms of trade mechanically produces a larger krone offer rather than a larger krone bid.

factors_changed.factor: 5: External Balance & Terms of Trade - strategic
factors_changed.reason: The commodity forward path is now explicitly bearish: J.P. Morgan at USD 80 for the fourth quarter and USD 78 at year end, the EIA at approximately USD 85 for the third quarter, both OPEC and the IEA cutting 2026 demand forecasts, and OPEC-plus completing its supply rollback in September. The structural surplus is unchanged; the direction of the commodity complex is not.

The evidence base for a downward revision to the published path accumulated through August - a second benign core print, a mainland GDP miss, house prices falling markedly, capacity utilisation drifting down and an import-weighted krone at a four-year high, which is disinflationary in Norges Bank's own reaction function.

Three Monetary Policy Reports now fall inside the horizon and the direction of successive revisions is genuinely unpredictable given the wage-frame counterweight, so guidance becomes a source of volatility rather than of direction.

Global fiscal differentiation became an active FX factor during August, with United States debt passing USD 40 trillion and Norwegian ten-year yields sitting 71.2 basis points below United Kingdom levels despite a 50 basis point higher policy rate. The stance strengthens while the confidence falls, because the transmission is now directional but less certain.

The backdrop is unchanged and still supportive, but the 16 September Summary of Economic Projections is now inside the tactical window and three hawkish FOMC dissents on 29 July make an upward revision to the dots a live risk.

Unchanged in both stance and confidence. Credit is tighter and the VIX lower than a month ago, but from these levels the six-month distribution is skewed against the krone given its asymmetric downside beta.

conviction_change.explanation: Neither conviction level changed, but the tactical STANCE flipped from Bullish to Bearish, so the same conviction number now expresses the opposite view. The tactical weighted score moved from plus 0.19 to minus 0.1130 - a swing of 0.30 - driven almost entirely by Flows and Positioning moving from Neutral to Bearish and by Policy and Rates losing its positive contribution. The strategic score fell from plus 0.361 to plus 0.2230 while the stance and conviction held, as the External Balance and Guidance factors moved to Neutral and were only partly replaced by Fiscal moving to Bullish. The G10 plus SGD ranking fell from 3 to 6 tactically and from 2 to 3 strategically.

new_catalysts: The Norges Bank October foreign exchange transaction announcement on 30 September 2026, which determines whether the September reversal was a regime or a one-month artefact. This did not exist as a catalyst a month ago because the reversal had not happened.

The 10 September 2026 European Central Bank meeting elevated from a routine decision to the single most consequential scheduled event for the krone's carry, on a hike probability that moved from unremarkable to approximately 80 per cent at the cited source.
The 16 September 2026 FOMC Summary of Economic Projections entering the tactical window, made material by the three hawkish dissents recorded on 29 July 2026.
The completion of the OPEC-plus voluntary-cut rollback with a final 188,000 barrel per day increase in September 2026.

The autumn Norwegian wage settlements, which will determine whether the 4.4 per cent front-line framework passes through and therefore whether core inflation stabilises in the mid-twos or continues falling.

seasonality.pattern: The only genuinely seasonal pattern in the krone is not a calendar effect in the usual sense but the annual rhythm of Norges Bank's foreign exchange transactions on behalf of the government, which is set by the interaction of petroleum tax receipts and the non-oil budget deficit and which is re-announced monthly. Petroleum tax instalments fall in even-numbered months, which produces a recurring pattern of corporate krone buying around those dates that partially offsets the official flow.
seasonality.relevance_window: Directly relevant to the tactical horizon: the September schedule is already published and effective from 1 September 2026, and the October schedule is announced at 10:00 on 30 September 2026, inside the strategic horizon.
seasonality.historical_magnitude: The swing between adjacent months is routinely of the order of NOK 300 to 700 million per day on the government leg; the current reversal of NOK 650 million per day is at the large end of that historical range but is not unprecedented.
seasonality.current_alignment: Currently adverse to the krone. The seasonal and fiscal drivers are aligned against the currency in September for the first time this year, and the offsetting corporate tax-payment flow is itself boosted by the higher oil price, which is the partial hedge embedded in the mechanism.

assumptions: Provenance convention. Figures drawn from the pipeline data cache are dated in the text with their as-of date and are recorded here rather than in the citation list, per pipeline convention. Everything else carries a numbered citation. No inline provenance tags are used anywhere in the prose.

DOCUMENTED GAP - implied volatility. No free, reliably dated quote for 1-month or 3-month EUR/NOK or USD/NOK implied volatility, the 1-year implied volatility percentile, the 25-delta risk reversal or the volatility term structure could be obtained. The iv_1m, iv_3m and iv_percentile_1y fields are ZERO PLACEHOLDERS and must not be read as market levels; the vol_term_structure enumeration is a schema default rather than an observation. Every volatility statement in this dossier uses cached realised volatility instead. The same gap was recorded for sterling, the euro and the franc in this cycle.

DOCUMENTED GAP - CFTC positioning. The Norwegian krone is not a CFTC-reportable Commitments of Traders market. CME does list a Norwegian krone futures contract, but the krone does not appear in the Commitments of Traders financial futures reports this pipeline consumes and the latest cached tranche of 2026-08-11 carries no krone line. Every CFTC field in the positioning block is a structural placeholder. Substitutes used: the Norges Bank pre-announced transaction schedule, 52-week range and close percentiles from the price store, and reported corporate oil-tax flow.

DOCUMENTED GAP - cross-currency basis. No quoted Norwegian krone basis, and no benchmark 3-month EUR/USD or JPY/USD basis, was obtainable. The NOK/USD figure of approximately minus 6 basis points and the NOK/EUR figure of approximately minus 10 basis points are DERIVED from the cached futures-implied roll premia of 56.5 and 189.8 basis points against policy differentials of 62.5 and 200 basis points. They are derivations, not quotes.

DOCUMENTED GAP - forward points. No free quoted source for USD/NOK forward points exists. All three outrights - 9.3480, 9.3569 and 9.3700 - and the corresponding points of plus 43, plus 132 and plus 263 pips are DERIVED from the cached 56.5 basis point futures-implied roll premium on an actual-over-365 basis at 30, 91 and 182 days, and are flagged as such.

DOCUMENTED GAP - Norwegian 2-year yield. Norges Bank publishes generic yields at 3, 6 and 12 months and 3, 5, 7 and 10 years, but no 2-year. The 4.56 per cent used in the sovereign yield block and in the 2s10s calculation is INTERPOLATED between the 12-month at 4.564 per cent and the 3-year at 4.561 per cent and is labelled indicative throughout.

DOCUMENTED GAP - I-44 index level. The level of Norges Bank's import-weighted I-44 krone index could not be obtained. Only the qualitative statement that it is at its strongest since autumn 2022 and up approximately 8.5 per cent year to date is available. The BIS real effective exchange rate is used as the trade-weighted measure throughout.

DOCUMENTED GAP - Norwegian sovereign CDS. No Norwegian sovereign credit default swap quote was obtainable. Norwegian CDS is illiquid and rarely quoted, which is itself informative about perceived credit risk.

DOCUMENTED GAP - peer core inflation. Preferred core inflation measures for Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Switzerland and Sweden were absent from the cached vintage store and were not independently sourced. Cached OECD or HICP headline vintages are repeated in the core column of the macro comparison table and are explicitly labelled as such in each affected row.

DOCUMENTED GAP - purchasing power parity. No free purchasing-power-parity source was obtainable. The PPP deviation table is a REER-RELATIVE PROXY, computed as the Norwegian BIS real effective exchange rate divided by each peer's, minus one, and it is stated as such in every row. It is not a purchasing-power-parity fair value. The NOK/JPY row of plus 53.94 per cent is a proxy artefact created by a depressed Japanese REER of 65.3 and is not tradeable.

BEST AVAILABLE, FLAGGED - current account. The Norwegian current account of 15.59 per cent of GDP is the point-in-time OECD 2026-Q1 vintage dated 2026-07-31 from the cached vintage store. It is contested by a Trading Economics calendar-2025 reading of 14.20 per cent computed on a different basis. The conclusion that Norway runs the largest surplus in the set is unaffected by which figure is used.

BEST AVAILABLE, FLAGGED - BIS REER. The BIS real effective exchange rate set is for the 2026-06 period, roughly 63 days before the valuation date and marginally outside the strategic freshness window. It could not be re-retrieved at that vintage. Its five-year historical percentile of approximately 70 is an EXPLICIT ESTIMATE; the cache carries only the level and the one-year change.

BEST AVAILABLE, FLAGGED - end-July Bund and the monthly spread change. The approximately 3.20 per cent German 10-year level used to compute the monthly change in the NGB-Bund spread is carried from the previous cycle's dossier, as is the corresponding end-July Norwegian generic of approximately 4.45 per cent, which together give a prior spread of approximately plus 125 basis points and roughly 12 basis points of compression to the current plus 112.8. The previous cycle recorded plus 129 basis points using a secondary 4.49 per cent Norwegian quote rather than the Norges Bank primary generic; the current spread is computed on matched 31 August 2026 closes and supersedes it.

BEST AVAILABLE, FLAGGED - Goldman Sachs forecast. The Goldman Sachs EUR/NOK 10.50 call is dated 30 May 2026, 94 days before the valuation date and outside both the 30-day tactical and 60-day strategic freshness windows. It is retained because it is one of only three published house forecasts obtainable for the pair and because its level coincides with a structural round number.

BEST AVAILABLE, FLAGGED - Brent level. Brent is quoted at USD 95.19 at the 1 September 2026 close in the figure carried into this build, giving plus 7.9 per cent against the cached 25 August level of USD 88.24. A re-check of the cited source on 2 September 2026 shows an intraday print of USD 95.02 on 1 September and a prior-day close nearer USD 94.65, which would give plus 7.3 per cent. The level is therefore dispersed within roughly half a dollar and is marked best available and flagged; the direction, a sharp geopolitical bid into September, is not in question. No factor confidence was adjusted for this, because the analytical conclusion is unchanged at either level.

BEST AVAILABLE, FLAGGED - ECB hike probability. The approximately 80 per cent market-implied probability of a 25 basis point European Central Bank hike on 10 September 2026 is the figure at the cited source. A re-check on 2 September 2026 returned 86 to 99 per cent from other vendors. The level is dispersed and is flagged; the direction - that the European Central Bank is the more likely hawkish mover and that the differential compresses - holds at any figure in that range.

STALE - cached sovereign 10-year series. The cached IRLTLT01 sovereign 10-year series are MONTHLY and as at 2026-06-01, roughly 92 days old, which breaches both the 30-day tactical and 60-day strategic freshness windows. They are superseded for Norway by the Norges Bank daily generic series and for Germany, the United Kingdom and Japan by current dated quotes. They are RETAINED as-is, and explicitly dated, for Switzerland, Canada, Australia and Sweden, which drive four of the eight key spreads in the sovereign yield block.

STALE - other cached series. The BIS REER period is 2026-06 (63 days). The latest cached CFTC tranche is 2026-08-11 (21 days) and carries no krone line, so it is not used for any figure in this dossier. The cached CBPOL_NO policy rate series is monthly as at 2026-07-01 but reconciles exactly with the 13 August 2026 Norges Bank press release. The cached OECD Norwegian CPI vintage of 3.09 per cent for 2025-Q4 is three quarters stale and is superseded throughout by the July 2026 Statistics Norway print. The Federal Reserve decision of 29 July (34 days) and the European Central Bank decision of 23 July (40 days) are outside the tactical window but are the most recent decisions in existence.

Methodological choice - carry-to-volatility denominator. Every carry-to-volatility ratio in this dossier is stated as annualised carry in percentage points divided by 60-day REALISED volatility read directly from the cached derived pair files, annualised on 252 from the weekday-only price store. Realised volatility is never recomputed and cross volatility is never constructed from two dollar legs. No implied-volatility-based ratio is given alongside, because no quoted implied volatility was obtainable.

Methodological choice - primary pair and conventions. EUR/NOK is treated as the primary pair for market structure, valuation and level discussion because it carries the deepest liquidity and the tightest link to the dominant rate spread, while USD/NOK is used for the forward-versus-spot decomposition and for all payoff arithmetic because the derived forward points exist only for that pair. Performance figures are stated from the krone's perspective: a fall in EUR/NOK is reported as krone strength.

Methodological choice - central bank dates. All central-bank decision dates come from the pipeline's authoritative calendar file and were never web-searched. Singapore has no policy rate by design; the Monetary Authority of Singapore operates an S$NEER band reviewed semi-annually, and the SGD policy rate and spread fields are null throughout rather than zero.

Interpretive choice - the wage frame. The 4.4 per cent figure from the 12 April 2026 front-line settlement is characterised throughout as the front-line model's expected average for the year - the benchmark against which subsequent public and private settlements are negotiated - and NOT as a hard legal ceiling. The earlier characterisation as a ceiling overstated its binding force.
